clue.text: Coastal feature Spooner's crew went under?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words that follow are exchanged

parts.note: a crew of musicians or workers can be a band
a ship that went under sank

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what happened to a boat's crew off the coast, with a sly question mark.
explanation.walkthrough: BAND SANK, with the initial letters exchanged, becomes SAND BANK.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge of sand built up offshore by currents is a typical feature of a coastline.

clue.text: Soldiers locking up deserter without charge

indicators.note: to lock up something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
a rat is someone who deserts a cause, as rats leave a sinking ship

explanation.surface: Troops detain an absconder and release him without pressing any charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks military or legal, but here it means a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given for nothing, free of any fee or payment, is gratis.

clue.text: Stop benefit rejected by parent and child

indicators.note: rejected here means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to aid is to benefit or help
pa is an informal word for father
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A parent and child turn down a benefit payment, calling a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' is the noun: an organ stop, the principal stop being the diapason.
explanation.definitionFit: On an organ the diapason is one of the main stops, a set of pipes the player draws on.

clue.text: Early form of life cultivated by Rome?

indicators.note: something cultivated has been worked over and changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks whether some early life form was grown or nurtured by ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: An organism in its first stage of development, before birth or hatching, is an embryo.

clue.text: Article by trainee reporter, one from West Indies …

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: a cub reporter is a newcomer learning the trade
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A news piece written by a junior journalist who comes from the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is a Caribbean island, so a native of it is a person from the West Indies.

clue.text: … feature article digested by rail workers ahead of time

indicators.note: ahead of puts the first piece in front of the second
something digested is taken inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: linemen maintain railway track
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Continues the previous clue: a feature story eaten up by railway staff before its deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: A lineament is a distinctive feature or outline, especially of a face.

clue.text: Non-involvement in sale is moving female in old country

indicators.note: moving letters around rearranges them
in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: Zaire is the former name of the Democratic Republic of the Congo

explanation.surface: Staying out of a sale, while a woman travels within some former nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase names a policy of leaving things alone, especially the state staying out of the economy.

clue.text: Uncouth goodie — one in suit with lace collar, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us a word is said out loud, giving a different spelling

parts.note: a ruff is a frilled starched collar, often of lace
a diamond is a card in one of the four suits

explanation.surface: A rough-mannered good guy, perhaps dressed in a suit with a lace collar.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with a good heart but unpolished manners is called by this idiom.

clue.text: Transmit from shed by minor thoroughfare

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: a B road is a secondary road in Britain
a snake that sheds its skin has cast it

explanation.surface: Broadcasting from a shed beside a country lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a hut; it is the verb meaning cast off. A B road is a minor British road.
explanation.definitionFit: To send out a programme or signal by radio or television is to broadcast it.

clue.text: Worthless information about first king of Ethiopia?

indicators.note: first puts the reversed piece at the front
about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
U/S, short for unserviceable, means useless or worthless

explanation.surface: Dismissive facts about Ethiopia's original monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is not part of the definition: it says the reversal leads. Negus was the Ethiopian royal title, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Negus was the title of the rulers of Ethiopia, whose emperor was the king of kings.

clue.text: Game stuffed with old English herb

indicators.note: something stuffed with another has it inside

parts.note: brag is a card game like poker

explanation.surface: Game birds stuffed with a traditional English herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like meat for stuffing; it is the card game brag.
explanation.definitionFit: Borage is a blue-flowered plant whose leaves are used in cooking and drinks.

clue.text: Lineage of female politician endlessly pursuing healthy activity

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so the earlier piece leads

parts.note: PE is physical education
Di is a woman's name

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a Green is a member of an environmentalist party

explanation.surface: The family history of a woman in politics who is always chasing fitness.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedigree is a recorded line of ancestry, so it means the same as descent or family line.

clue.text: Trick hospital department, getting rebuke

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat
a rap on the knuckles is a rebuke

explanation.surface: Someone tricks a hospital ward and gets reprimanded.
explanation.definitionFit: To trick someone into a compromising position is to ensnare them in a trap.

clue.text: Daydream? It's unknown in a stager's travels

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other
travels means the letters wander into a new order

parts.note: z is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An actor on tour has idle dreams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travels' rearranges A STAGER to STARGAE; Z goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To stare dreamily into space, or gaze at the stars, is a cryptic picture of daydreaming.

clue.text: Take advantage of something chewed over in bishop's place

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: cud is food chewed again by cattle

explanation.surface: Exploiting something mulled over at a bishop's residence.
explanation.definitionFit: To seduce someone is to lead them astray, taking advantage of them sexually.

clue.text: Almost forks out pounds for book close at hand

indicators.note: forks out means pays away, so a letter is given up
for means in exchange, so a new letter replaces it

parts.note: nearly means almost
l is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Someone nearly pays up for a book that is handy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forks out' and 'for' swap L in NEARLY for B.
explanation.definitionFit: Something situated close by is within easy reach or not far away.

clue.text: Indoctrinate supporter's husband touring in western area

indicators.note: touring means going around, so these letters surround the others

parts.note: a bra is a supporter; with the possessive s it gives this

explanation.surface: A backer's husband on tour in the west tries to brainwash people.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAS plus H surrounds IN, W and A.
explanation.definitionFit: To indoctrinate someone is to force a belief on them by persistent pressure.

clue.text: Worried in case locals like some of Soane's buildings?

indicators.note: worried means shaken about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Residents fret that something will happen to their architectural heritage.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir John Soane was a Georgian English architect, designer of the Bank of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Soane worked in a revived classical style, drawing on Greek and Roman forms.

clue.text: University doctor invited into academy dance

indicators.note: invited into means placed inside

parts.note: RA is the Royal Academy
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A university medic invited into an academy to dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance with rhythmic hip movement.

clue.text: Appellation (sound) Heather mostly used for condiment

indicators.note: sound in brackets says this word is to be spoken and spelt as heard

parts.note: a term is a name or appellation

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: erica is the botanical name for heather

explanation.surface: A name, plus heather, used to make a seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmeric is a yellow spice, a seasoning used in curries.

clue.text: Old actor with house in Kent — one doing a stretch in Oxford?

definitions.text: one doing a stretch in Oxford?

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: Kent is a county in the south-east of England, SE
Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: An old actor's Kent house, and someone serving time in Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' is not the city but an Oxford, a laced shoe. 'stretch' sounds like prison time.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe tree is a form put inside a shoe to keep its shape, stretching it.

clue.text: During time in school Italian wine's produced on and off

parts.note: in means during
a term is a period of the school year
it is short for Italian vermouth
tent is a Spanish red wine; the 's is is, a link

explanation.surface: An Italian wine made in school occasionally.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that stops and starts at irregular intervals happens off and on.

clue.text: Gnome at home in more decorative surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means enclosing the other piece

parts.note: fancier means more ornate
in means at home

explanation.surface: A garden gnome sits indoors in more ornate setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gnome' means not a garden ornament but a 'gnome of Zurich', a Swiss banker.
explanation.definitionFit: The gnomes of Zurich was a phrase for Swiss bankers, so a gnome is a money man.

clue.text: Likely story head of art put out about ex-pupil

indicators.note: about means around, so these letters surround the other
a letter that is put out is thrown out of the word, so it is taken away

parts.note: a parable is a story with a moral

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter

parts.note: an OB is an old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A probable story of an art teacher fired over an old student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' takes the first A from PARABLE to give PRABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Probable means likely to happen or be true.

clue.text: Tyrant's car runs into Burmese, perhaps

parts.note: auto is short for automobile

indicators.note: a car that runs into something ends up inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a Burmese is a breed of cat
r is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A dictator's car runs into a Burmese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tyrant's' is Tyrant has; 'Burmese' is the cat, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocrat rules with absolute power, like a despot.

clue.text: She gave advice, say, about climbing in Alpine peaks?

parts.note: eg means for example, say

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means read upwards

parts.note: re means about

indicators.note: peaks are tops, the first letters

explanation.surface: A woman gave advice, for example about mountaineering in the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: In Roman legend Egeria was a nymph who counselled King Numa.
explanation.definitionFit: Egeria advised King Numa, so the name now means a female counsellor.

clue.text: Ascetic French art environment academic finally abandons

parts.note: es is French for 'you are', thou art

indicators.note: abandons means leaves out

parts.note: a scene is a setting

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter

explanation.surface: French art about an environment that an academic finally abandons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is the old form of are, French ES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect at the time of Christ.

clue.text: Take degree, having assimilated core of religious doctrine

indicators.note: having assimilated means taking in

parts.note: to do a course is to take it
an MA is a Master of Arts degree

indicators.note: core of picks the middle letter

explanation.surface: Take a degree having studied religious doctrine.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a set of principles laid down by an authority as true.
